result.title: The psychophysics of affect in large language models
result.comment: 64 pages (26 main text, 25 Supplementary Information, 13 GUIDE-LLM reporting checklist), 5 figures. Code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23772352 ; data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23556542
result.summary: Good decisions often require considering how outcomes will feel. Yet large language models (LLMs) increasingly enter decision workflows, despite little being known about how they map outcomes to feelings or use those mappings in choice. We tested how LLMs anticipated gambling or stock-trading outcomes would feel and whether they incorporated these ratings into choice. When outcomes were rated in isolation, ratings exhibited diminishing sensitivity to magnitude, resembling human value functions; but models rated gains more intensely than equivalent losses, an inversion of canonical loss aversion we call silicon gain amplification. When outcomes were rated together, enabling direct comparison, ratings linearised. In choice, the gain-loss asymmetry largely disappeared, and models' own ratings did not reliably explain their choices better than monetary utility did. These findings reveal malleable mappings from outcomes to affect, raising questions about whether and how agentic LLMs should incorporate anticipated feelings into decisions.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文用心理物理学范式测试 LLM 对赌博、股票交易结果的情感预期评分，发现单独评分时呈递减敏感性且收益强于损失（「硅基增益放大」），并列评分时趋于线性，并检验这些自评能否解释模型的实际选择。
AI.relevance_reason: 模型内部「结果—情感」映射的可塑性与自评解释力不足，可能启发 LVR 中对 latent 状态是否真正参与答案与取舍决策、以及自评与行为是否一致的核查思路。
